spine.claim: Consumers believe they make rational buying choices, but subconscious mental shortcuts dictate every purchase.
Context, social proof, and distinctiveness override pure price and quality comparisons.
Admitting flaws and leveraging anchoring can turn perceived product weaknesses into irresistible strengths.
Friction and scarcity create physical and emotional pressure points that dictate market winners.
We never buy products solely for what they are, but for the mental relief of letting a cognitive shortcut decide.
